cut.name: The Root Tunnel
cut.evidence: No active entity or switch: a thorn gap and climbable high bank, using only travel/jump/grab inputs. Wall climbing was taught by White Flowers in W1. Keep the arrival/rest function if replacing it.

cut.name: The Called Name
cut.evidence: Two bells and twenty cyan phase tiles extend the same dash/strike parity lesson as Mirror Thicket; Rootbound Passage immediately adds the more consequential pod-plus-bell combined cut. A new phase puzzle can occupy this middle repetition without removing the first bell lesson.

cut.name: Drop Yard
cut.evidence: One four-tile vertical lift rises eleven tiles beside a thorned far bank. The saved route includes a 56-frame idle ride and no blade interaction; Chainwake Camp already establishes weight-triggered lift travel, while The Hoist follows with its new momentum lesson.

cut.name: The Choir Flue
cut.evidence: One four-tile-wide updraft and one pod beside a tall thorned wall; the tape has one downward strike and then a long held up/right exit. The preceding Catcher Span already combines draft, spring and two pods, so this late single-pod reprise is a stronger replacement candidate than the wind introductions.

cut.name: Gatehouse Hearth
cut.evidence: The lantern starts inside a sealed overhead pocket directly above its plate; the eighteen door tiles are already held open. The saved tape contains only rightward walking/jumping and no pickup/throw. W1 Gatehouse already taught active plate weighting. Good slot for an early cargo puzzle that requires the player to establish the state.

cut.name: Eastern Crown
cut.evidence: The jailer/gate sits in a sealed side pocket while the main road descends around it. The four-segment route uses only left and jump, including 144 frames held left; no combat input. Keep the region arrival, but the actual shield/back and parry lessons are the next two rooms.

cut.name: The Bellows
cut.evidence: Two vertically staged pressure pods repeat Hush Engine’s newly introduced reversal/refill in a second launch. A replacement can combine that known resource with another decision, provided it still supplies a forgiving second pod practice before the jailer combinations.

cut.name: The Stair Foot
cut.evidence: A six-tile heat slab lies flush with otherwise continuous row-18 floor. Saved tape is exactly right 65, idle 55, right 133; no jump/dash/weapon input. It revisits the first cycle lesson after the multi-slab descent. Keep a short arrival-safe seam if replacing this post-sequence breather.

cut.name: The Casting Line
cut.evidence: One lantern, one plate and a leftward belt solve a remote held hatch; there are no moulds, anvils or hazards in the map. The later Feeder adds a cast stop to the same belt/cargo/plate problem. Strong place to substitute a cargo machinery puzzle while keeping belt introduction in Deep Stair.

cut.name: The Unreachable Line
cut.evidence: Two shallow thorn beds in the row-18 road and one overhead stone block; no prism or other active device. Tape uses only walking/jump/dash. At W12, this repeats the W1 movement lesson immediately before the actual gravity introduction.

cut.name: The Quiet Threshold
cut.evidence: Two five-tile thorn beds and a short solid block on a steady floor; no prisms, gravity cargo, crystal or switch. It follows Void Fissure’s repeated gravity reversals. An obvious low-complexity slot, although its breather/region-exit purpose should be retained.

cut.name: The Vigil Crossing
cut.evidence: Three tears carry the knight through a thorn field; there is no spent ledge, pod or crystal in the map. The six-segment saved tape revisits chain transfer after Tear to Tear already adds a disappearing perch. Keep the pre-boss transition but give its route a second consequential resource.

cut.name: The Audience Hall
cut.evidence: Two-body crown occupancy repeats Borrowed Body after the more involved momentum swap and one-way-tear return rooms. Its map has only gate tiles and seven floor thorns beside the echo/crown state. Preserve a last crown rehearsal before the seals, but a bank replacement can ask more than leaving the echo on the low mark.

cut.name: Westbound
cut.evidence: One cart on seventeen rail tiles, one refill crystal and a tall exit over spikes. The decision is a conventional second dash after dismount, whereas subsequent carts change bell state, portal momentum or cargo/enemy jobs. Preserve the westward road turn and receiving checkpoint if substituting.

cut.name: The Colony Road
cut.evidence: A single five-tile thorn bed and a three-tile-high block on dry continuous floor; no tide or float. The ten-segment tape contains only ordinary movement after Landfall’s multi-entity flight. Strong geometry-based replacement slot if retaining a short safe transition into the Colony.

cut.name: Beyond the Watch
cut.evidence: One five-tile thorn bed plus a three-tile-high block; no watch light, smoke or moving cover. It repeats the same plain transition family as W17 Colony Road, one tile farther right. Keep its seam/checkpoint but it need not consume a whole challenge slot.

cut.name: The Sun Line
cut.evidence: Two shutter tiles and a tear span a single thorn field; only four held-input segments are saved. It revisits shutter departure timing without the mirror preparation in Beat and Glass. Good slot for two linked timing/arrival decisions while retaining the Sun Line’s clear beam cue.

cut.name: The Engine Road
cut.evidence: Nine phase tiles over a thorn road, toggled by dash and tied to beam shade. Switchback Engine already teaches that same dual effect; the later room adds jumps but no new object role. Prefer a replacement with a meaningful state return, while preserving the region’s phase/light identity.

cut.name: The Torn Mile
cut.evidence: Three tears deliver to cracked perches before a last super; the next Muster Yard adds a crystal to the same tear/perch/super chain. A new room can replace this intermediate chain while retaining the first tear lesson in Camp Echo.

cut.name: The Hollow Crown
cut.evidence: A tear, one pod and eight cracked tiles form a lift/cut/low-launch sequence. All three verbs have been introduced earlier, while this room does not use the chapter’s lashes or resin wind. A replacement can combine low launch with a more consequential timed arrival; retain any attached secret host.

cut.name: The Unlit Well
cut.evidence: A descending solid staircase with no hazard glyph, enemy or device; the entire saved route is [200, left]. The hint explicitly calls it a breath before the courts. This is the clearest Fractured low-complexity slot, but keep some safe boss preparation rather than filling every breather.

cut.name: The Counterweight Rise
cut.evidence: One rising lift launches to a cracked lip and then a second cracked sill; the main demand is two supers in succession. The first lift/ultra route and Relay Gantry already teach lift momentum and unstable arrival, while Last Gantry is the fuller combination. Preserve vertical/horizontal seam orientation.

cut.name: The Cracked Rain-Catcher
cut.evidence: Four cracked cups alternate between polished walls; the repeated action is landing and immediately wallbouncing to the next cup. It develops an already established wallbounce chain, whereas the following lung rooms add changing wind direction. Replace with a distinctive wallbounce combination, not an ordinary jump room.

cut.name: The Cracked Shaft
cut.evidence: Exactly five separate three-tile fault ledges climb a shaft, with no projectile, moving cover or other object. The author source describes each as a jump and dash from the last. Keep Seam as the first fault lesson; this second single-system repetition can become a broader fault application.

cut.name: Mason’s Quarter
cut.evidence: One anchored portal crosses the masons’ full wall from fault footing; the palette/fault pressure changes, but the portal topology repeats Base Mason’s Quarter. A stronger portal/cargo state puzzle can go here without removing portal training from W6.

cut.name: The Bellows
cut.evidence: Two pressure pods with shade and thorned walls repeat the Hush Engine launch/refill, before subsequent rooms add jailer facing and cells. Keep Hush Engine’s first pod practice; replace this duplicate family with another pressure-pod interaction if matching bank material exists.

cut.name: Muster Engine
cut.evidence: One feather at the top of a draft, shade pursuit and no fault glyph despite a fault option. This preserves the Base Engine’s single wind/feather idea rather than adding another object state. A more developed aerial resource chain can fit before Crown without taking away the introductory ice rooms.

cut.name: The Glazed Gallery
cut.evidence: Four full-height panes, two crystals and one four-tile fault perch; the core task is repeated left/right remapping with refill management. Pane Stair already teaches four-pane traversal on fault ledges. This later pane-only reprise is a stronger replacement candidate than the first mirror lesson.

cut.name: The Cooling Road
cut.evidence: One four-tile fault perch and one four-tile heat slab, with no mirror or shade. It reprises the basic temporary-floor handoff after Ember Door already chains three slabs with a pane. Good compact slot for a more causal timing problem.

cut.name: The Hot Line
cut.evidence: Two anvils, two full panes and one three-tile fault perch form another stepping-stone line. The previous Slag Heap already combines anvils, glass, fault and shade with a meaningful low roof. Prefer replacing this repeated forward line before the richer Overlook.

cut.name: Polarity Gauntlet
cut.evidence: Four prism crossings across short fault slabs with one pane; no cargo or held gate despite the former Drop-Lock ancestry. Prism to Prism already asks for repeated flips and refills. A replacement could restore a causal gravity/object task to a world dominated by traversal strings.

cut.name: The Thrown Line
cut.evidence: A forward chain of one-way tears over thorns, with no fault perch, cargo, enemy, tally or second resource in the room. It repeats sequential mouth-to-mouth transfer after Spent Seam already establishes one-way commitment.

cut.name: The Drowning Stair
cut.evidence: Nine spent foothold tiles and six fault tiles climb with the shades behind; this repeats Long Drowning’s consumed footholds and pursuit but lacks its return over the earlier route. Keep that stronger return problem and use the later climb slot for a different shared-state application.

cut.name: Shade on the Line
cut.evidence: One cart on three rail tiles hands into a long fault/tear chain with shade. Two Carts already ties moving seats to shade pressure, and Blinking Line adds a route-relevant arrival phase. This later single-seat continuation is a lower-confidence repetition candidate.

cut.name: The Staple
cut.evidence: One ring, one pane, one three-tile fault perch and tear transfer repeat the resources already used through Glass Chain, Glass Seam and Glass Between. Unlike Long Chain there is no rope-length-dependent tally. Replace this simple resource chain before the adjustable-rope puzzle.

cut.name: Under the Spray
cut.evidence: No tern or other enemy is present: fault footing, a low roof, a tear and shade form a super-to-rise transfer. The later Landfall really combines float, moth and ring. Prefer the latter for the enemy lesson; this former enemy slot can regain an interactive timing target.

cut.name: Two Shadows
cut.evidence: A short line of smoke-covered fault stones with a lamp ahead and shade behind. Lamplight/Smoke already establish shelter departure and Glance adds shade across three lanes. This later one-line restatement has fewer distinct object jobs than the neighbouring Release/Watch combinations.

cut.name: Panes
cut.evidence: Two panes, six phase tiles, six fault tiles and a tear, but no beam/shutter field. It repeats remapped dash parity after Low Light and Beat without making a light change matter. A bank replacement should restore a physical light/state consequence rather than merely add another pane.

cut.name: The Hours
cut.evidence: Four timed tears over thorn curtains onto six fault tiles; no beam, portal or phase field. It repeats the sequenced tear-clock family established in W33/W35. Keep the chapter opening synthesis in Court; this early reprise can be replaced by a fresh timing problem.
